summary: How the browser UI, the Vite dev proxy, the FastAPI backend, local storage and the LLM providers work together end to end.

architecture.style: Client–server web app run locally: React SPA → Vite dev proxy → one FastAPI process (+ a subprocess for training) → SQLite and files, with optional paid LLM APIs
architecture.summary: The browser loads a React single-page app from the Vite dev server on :5173. Every page talks to the backend through one small fetch helper (api.ts) using relative /api/... paths. Vite forwards those to FastAPI on :8000, so the browser never sees API keys and never needs CORS. FastAPI routes each request to one lab module, which reads and writes SQLite/files and may call DeepSeek or Groq. Long work (LoRA training) runs in a separate process, and the page polls for progress.

deployables.name: Vite dev server
deployables.what: Serves the React app on :5173 and proxies /api to the backend

deployables.name: make dev
deployables.what: Starts both halves together; Ctrl-C stops both

unknowns: No production build hosting or deployment config: the app is only run locally with `make dev`.
No authentication: roles (analyst, reviewer…) are chosen in the UI and enforced by the backend, but nothing proves who the user is.
A production build (`vite build`) has no proxy; how /api would be served in that setup isn't defined in the repo.

groups.name: Browser
groups.what: Runs on the user's machine in the browser tab

groups.name: Dev server
groups.what: Vite: serves the UI and forwards API calls

groups.name: Backend server
groups.what: The FastAPI process and its subprocesses

groups.name: Local data
groups.what: SQLite databases and files on disk

groups.name: External services
groups.what: Paid LLM APIs and downloaded models

nodes.label: React app (SPA)
nodes.what: The single-page app: one layout with a sidebar, an overview page, and one page per lab.
nodes.why: It turns each lab's JSON into something you can click, compare and read. Without it you'd use curl or the /docs page.
nodes.analogy: The dashboard of a car: it shows what the engine (backend) is doing and gives you the controls.
responsibilities: Call the API and show loading/error states

nodes.label: index.html + main.tsx
nodes.what: Sets dark mode before paint from localStorage, then mounts <App/> into #root.

nodes.label: App.tsx (routes)
nodes.what: Maps URLs like /evidence-atlas or /tracelens to page components inside the shared Layout.

nodes.label: Layout.tsx (shell + status)
nodes.what: Sidebar navigation for the seven workspaces, theme toggle, and a provider status badge loaded from /api/status.

nodes.label: api.ts (fetch + hooks)
nodes.what: One fetch wrapper that sends JSON, parses the reply and throws ApiError with the backend's error kind. Hooks: useApi (GET on mount), useAction (button calls), usePoll (repeat while a job runs).

nodes.label: ui.tsx (shared widgets)
nodes.what: Cards, stats, tabs, SVG charts and ErrorBox, which explains errors like 'no provider configured' in plain words.

nodes.label: Lab pages (×7 + Overview)
nodes.what: EvidenceAtlas, IntentForge, CacheCraft, TrustBoundary, SignalLoop, MissionReplay, TraceLens and Overview. Each calls only its own /api/<lab> routes.

nodes.label: Vite dev server :5173
nodes.what: Serves the app files with hot reload and forwards every /api request to the backend.
nodes.why: Because the browser only ever talks to :5173, there is no cross-origin problem and API keys stay on the server side.
nodes.analogy: A receptionist who passes your note to the back office so you never need its direct number.
responsibilities: Serve and hot-reload the React app

nodes.label: /api proxy
nodes.what: One config line: { "/api": "http://127.0.0.1:8000" }.

nodes.label: FastAPI backend :8000
nodes.what: One Python process. It validates each request with pydantic, routes it to the right lab, and converts failures into clear HTTP errors.
nodes.why: This is where every rule is enforced (roles, gates, guardrails). The UI only displays results; it can't bypass the backend.

nodes.label: App, CORS, /api/status
nodes.what: Creates the app, allows the dev origin, mounts routers, and serves /api/status (which providers are usable, which embedder).

nodes.label: Error handlers
nodes.what: ProviderUnavailable→409, ProviderError→502, PermissionError→403, ValueError→400. Secrets are scrubbed from the message.

nodes.label: 7 lab routers
nodes.what: /api/rag, /api/finetune, /api/cache, /api/guard, /api/feedback, /api/agents, /api/traces + /api/observability. Each declares pydantic request models.

nodes.label: Lab logic (p01–p07)
nodes.what: The actual pattern implementations (RAG pipeline, cache gateway, guardrail pipeline, …). See the 7-labs map for their insides.

nodes.label: Core: providers + tracing
nodes.what: The one LLM client and the span recorder every lab uses.

nodes.label: Job runner
nodes.what: Spawns training/evaluation as a separate process and tracks it with a pid file and log.

nodes.label: Training subprocess
nodes.what: A separate `python -m lab.p02_finetune.train` process that trains a LoRA adapter and writes progress to status.json. Needs the ML extras (torch).
nodes.why: Training takes minutes. Running it outside the API process keeps the UI responsive and frees memory when it ends.

nodes.label: SQLite var/lab.db
nodes.what: Shared database: spans, cache entries, guard log/approvals, feedback, agent runs, alerts.

nodes.label: Files: data/ + var/
nodes.what: Committed fixtures and runtime artefacts (datasets, adapters, results, job logs).

nodes.label: Browser localStorage
nodes.what: Stores only the light/dark theme choice.

nodes.label: .env (keys + flags)
nodes.what: API keys and LAB_* settings, read once at backend start. Never sent to the browser.

nodes.label: DeepSeek / Groq APIs
nodes.what: OpenAI-compatible chat APIs, used only when a key is set and LAB_OFFLINE is off.

nodes.label: Local HF models
nodes.what: MiniLM embeddings, cross-encoder and SmolLM2, downloaded once and run on CPU.

flows.name: Open the app
flows.description: How the page boots, picks a theme, and learns which providers are usable.

steps.text: A tiny inline script reads the saved theme before React loads, so the page doesn't flash white in dark mode.
React mounts and the router picks the page for the current URL inside the shared Layout.
The Layout asks for /api/status on mount (useApi).
Vite forwards the call to FastAPI on port 8000.
The reply says which providers are configured/usable, the embedder, and whether content capture is on. Keys themselves are never included.

flows.name: Ask a RAG question from the UI
flows.trigger: User clicks Ask in Evidence Atlas
flows.description: One full round trip: button → fetch → proxy → router → lab → SQLite/LLM → JSON → rendered answer.

steps.text: The page's useAction wraps the call so it can show a spinner and any error.
fetch sends JSON with POST to a relative URL, so it goes to the same origin (:5173).
Forwarded to FastAPI. Pydantic validates the body (e.g. question 3–500 chars) or returns 422.
The router calls the RAG pipeline, which opens a root span so the whole request is one trace.
Only if 'use LLM' is on and a key exists: the sources and question go to DeepSeek/Groq. Otherwise an offline extractive answer is used.
Each span is written to SQLite as it closes, with content hashed unless capture is enabled.
JSON comes back through the proxy; the page renders the answer, citations and per-passage scores, and can link the trace_id to TraceLens.

flows.name: Error path: LLM requested but no key
flows.trigger: User turns on 'use LLM' without a configured provider
flows.description: How a backend error becomes a helpful message in the UI.

steps.text: The pipeline raises ProviderUnavailable before doing any work.
The handler returns HTTP 409 with error kind 'provider_unavailable' and a secret-scrubbed detail.
api.ts throws ApiError carrying the kind; ErrorBox turns it into plain advice: switch off the LLM option or add a key to .env.

flows.name: Train a LoRA adapter and watch progress
flows.description: Long work runs in a subprocess; the page polls until it finishes.

steps.text: The page POSTs hyperparameters and switches polling on.
The route spawns the job; if one is already running it returns 409.
A new Python process starts training; the API replies right away with the run_id.
Every few steps the worker updates status.json with step, loss history and ETA.
usePoll calls GET /api/finetune/runs every 2 s while the job runs.
The route reads each run's status.json plus the log tail; when job_running turns false, polling stops.

flows.name: Human approval of a risky action
flows.trigger: TrustBoundary queues an outbound email; a reviewer approves it
flows.description: Friction by design: the backend re-checks policy against the reviewer's role before executing.

steps.text: The page sends the document for processing; risky actions come back as pending_approval.
The pending action is stored in guard_approvals instead of being executed.
The reviewer clicks approve/reject, sending their role.
Policy is re-checked for the reviewer's role; only then does the action run, and the decision is recorded.

flows.name: Inspect a trace in TraceLens
flows.trigger: User opens TraceLens and selects a trace
flows.description: Reads back the spans every other page's requests produced.

steps.text: The trace list is fetched with filters (module, status, search).
metrics.search groups spans by trace_id from the spans table.
Selecting a trace loads its full span tree (and optionally compares it with another).
The waterfall shows each step's latency, tokens, cost and status, so you can find exactly which step failed.
